# Options trading from zero

**Start with [your first tiny lesson](START_HERE.md).** This course teaches U.S. stock and ETF options to someone with no trading experience, in **10–15 minute study sessions**. You need a notebook and a basic calculator. Coding, a brokerage account and paid data are optional later tools.

The [beginner course](beginner/README.md) contains **64 lessons in eight modules**, with worked examples, fresh questions, folded answers, checkpoints, reviews and a final practical assessment. Learn one concept, try one problem, and stop for the day. Repeat a lesson whenever you need to.

## Your course app

The full application is in [course-app](course-app/README.md). It provides a lesson reader, server-graded quizzes, saved notes and progress, scheduled recall reviews, a practice payoff chart, a resource library and a downloadable learning record. Progress starts empty and changes only when you do the work. Your private hosted app uses ChatGPT sign-in.

The frontend uses React and TypeScript. The backend uses Vinext route handlers, Cloudflare Workers, D1 and Drizzle migrations. See the application README for running it locally and the verification record for the checks actually completed.

## What you will learn

| Part | Lessons | What you will be able to explain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Money and markets](beginner/01_MARKETS.md) | 01–08 | Shares, percentages, ETFs, prices and orders |
| [Option contracts](beginner/02_CONTRACTS.md) | 09–16 | Calls, puts, strike, expiry, premium and position direction |
| [Profit and loss](beginner/03_PROFIT.md) | 17–24 | Contract dollars, break-even, maximum loss and share obligations |
| [Option prices](beginner/04_PRICES.md) | 25–32 | Time, uncertainty and the Greeks without calculus |
| [Exercise and expiration](beginner/05_OPERATIONS.md) | 33–40 | Closing, exercise, assignment and the resulting cash and shares |
| [Strategies](beginner/06_STRATEGIES.md) | 41–48 | What simple positions accomplish and what they can lose |
| [Risk and decisions](beginner/07_RISK.md) | 49–56 | Position size, loss recovery, concentration, evidence and planning |
| [Practice](beginner/08_PRACTICE.md) | 57–64 | Quotes, paper orders, ledgers, review and an integrated capstone |

Use [How to study](HOW_TO_STUDY.md), the [review plan](beginner/REVIEW_PLAN.md), [workbook](beginner/WORKBOOK.md) and [glossary](beginner/GLOSSARY.md) when needed. None needs to be memorized before Lesson 1.

## After the beginner course

The existing [104-week advanced curriculum](COURSE.md), [four teaching volumes](LESSONS_01_FOUNDATIONS.md), [research lab](RESEARCH_LAB.md), [operations casebook](OPERATIONAL_CASEBOOK.md) and [Python labs](labs/README.md) remain available for deeper study. They are optional extensions, with their own prerequisites and projects.

Completion demonstrates learning and practice; it does not establish a profitable trading strategy or authorize live trading. Choosing to keep studying, use options only for understanding, or avoid options is a valid result.

## Verification

The [verification report](VERIFICATION_REPORT.md) records the **November 14, 2026** review, corrections, mathematical checks, application checks and limits. The [source library](SOURCES.md) links to SEC, OCC/OIC, FINRA, exchange and other primary materials. Examples use invented prices unless explicitly identified as observations. A course cannot establish that it is the best in the world or guarantee profits; this course aims for clear teaching, accurate mechanics and demonstrable understanding.

title: Options Research Lab
body:
# Options Research Lab

This lab turns an options idea into a decision that can be inspected, challenged, and reproduced. A profitable chart or a high win rate is not evidence of an edge by itself. For a historical contract-level performance claim, the research standard is **net performance under plausible execution and adverse market conditions, measured on data that did not choose the strategy**.

This is an educational research workflow for U.S. listed options. Sources rechecked October 26, 2026. It does not recommend a security, strategy, or position size. Contract rules, data products, fees, margin, and broker behavior must be checked again when a study is run.

Choose the evidence level **before** writing a confirmatory protocol: **A** validates accounting and chronology on explicitly synthetic cases; **B** compares published index histories and methodologies; **C** replays historical option contracts using suitable point-in-time data. Each level has a different defensible conclusion. Level A cannot measure market profitability. Level B cannot prove option-order fills from an index series. Level C can estimate historical net results under stated data and execution assumptions, then needs separate forward evidence. The [runnable apprenticeship](labs/README.md) supplies level A fixtures, expected behavior, and automated checks. Screen data access, licensing, timestamp fields, budget, and reproduction feasibility before committing to level C.

## The research record

Keep a versioned, append-only record for each experiment:

```text
research/<experiment-id>/
  hypothesis.md          # dated, written before inspecting test results
  evidence_level.md      # A/B/C, feasible data, source rights, permitted claim
  data_manifest.yaml     # source, license, timestamp, coverage, adjustments
  contract_rules.md      # A/C: exercise, settlement, multiplier, expiry
  methodology.md         # B: published index rules and unknown account fills
  code/                  # versioned ingestion and level-appropriate analysis
  tests/                 # A/C: payoff, chronology, fill, accounting checks
  runs/<run-id>/          # config, code commit, inputs hash, outputs, logs
  report.md              # results, failures, limitations, next decision
```

Use the files relevant to the chosen level. B needs published methodology and source series in place of a reconstructed contract ledger. Record the clock time and time zone of every market observation and simulated decision where applicable, and the release date of published series for B. Store raw data separately from cleaned data. Save the exact universe, data version, code commit, parameters, calendar, fees, and random seed used by each run as applicable. A second person should be able to rerun the report from the manifest. MIT's [Analytics of Finance](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/15-450-analytics-of-finance-fall-2010/pages/syllabus/) combines derivatives pricing, simulation, econometrics, estimation, and volatility modeling; its [notes and problem sets](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/15-450-analytics-of-finance-fall-2010/pages/lecture-notes/) are a useful technical standard for the lab.

## Study workflow

### 1. Write a falsifiable hypothesis first

Specify a claim appropriate to the evidence level. A/C specify the option universe, selection rule, entry and exit times, holding period, hedge rule, risk budget, and conditions expected to break the idea. B specifies published index and comparator series, methodologies, release dates, date alignment, and what would change the descriptive conclusion. State what result would make you reject the claim. Freeze the primary metric before viewing a genuinely reserved final segment. Record every parameter search, rejected variant, and change of mind; trying many versions and reporting only the winner inflates apparent performance. The [Probability of Backtest Overfitting](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2326253) explains why conventional holdout practices can fail after repeated strategy selection.

Example hypothesis template:

```text
Claim:
Economic reason someone would pay for this exposure:
Exact option and underlying universe, or B index/comparator series:
Observable inputs and when each becomes available:
Rules fixed before testing:
Primary outcome and benchmark:
Expected failure regimes:
Maximum parameter trials and decision rule:
Development / validation / genuinely untouched period, if available:
Evidence level, available data, and claims the data cannot support:
```

### 2. Build a point-in-time data set

For level C, first confirm a legally usable and affordable source. For each option observation retain the full contract identifier, underlying, expiration, strike, put/call, multiplier, deliverable, quote timestamp, bid, ask, sizes, volume, and open interest where supplied. Include contemporaneous underlying prices, distributions or dividends, rates, corporate actions, exchange calendar, and product-specific exercise and settlement terms. Reconstruct the **contracts that existed then** and the information visible at that time; do not select today's surviving symbols and project them backward. For level A, label every fixture synthetic and retain its generation rules and hashes. For level B, archive the published index series, current methodology, release dates, comparator series, and any methodology changes; do not fabricate the missing option quotes.

Reject or flag missing, stale, locked or crossed, zero-bid, impossible, and out-of-session quotes under written rules. Do not silently replace them with interpolated theoretical prices. Audit a random sample of raw rows against the vendor's source specification and manually reconstruct several option chains across ordinary days, earnings, dividends, splits, and expirations. Cboe's [EOD data specification](https://datashop.cboe.com/option-eod-summary) provides 15:45 ET and end-of-day NBBO snapshots; optional implied volatility and Greeks are calculated at the 15:45 snapshot. Its [intraday quote product](https://datashop.cboe.com/option-quote-intervals) provides interval snapshots. Confirm early-close timestamps, quote-size conventions, and whether the purchased product includes underlying index values; these vary by date and license. The [DataShop FAQ](https://datashop.cboe.com/faqs) notes that open interest is from the prior night's OCC report and that digit-bearing roots can identify adjusted, nonstandard options. [OCC volume and open-interest reports](https://www.theocc.com/market-data/market-data-reports/volume-and-open-interest/volume-query) can support cross-checks. Full historical option quotes generally require licensed data; a closing-price series alone is insufficient for a credible fill study.

**Data gate:** All levels identify source rights, observation dates, known missing fields, and the permitted claim. Level A publishes its synthetic rules, fixture hashes, and hand-checked cases. Level B reconciles the published index and comparator dates and explains methodology assumptions. Level C additionally publishes coverage by date and contract, missing and rejected quote counts, stale-quote rule, corporate-action treatment, and at least ten manually checked contract-days including one special-event case. Any unexplained C discrepancy in contract terms, observation time, or deliverable blocks the backtest.

### 3. Validate pricing and accounting before strategy results

Implement payoff and cash-flow accounting independently of the signal. Verify call and put payoff diagrams, put-call parity where its assumptions fit, the contract multiplier, fees, dividends, exercise/assignment, cash settlement or delivery, expirations, and hedges. Reconcile a hand-worked trade from entry to exit against code. Compare theoretical prices and Greeks with a second implementation; investigate differences in rate, dividend, calendar, exercise style, and volatility conventions. The original [Black–Scholes paper](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/260062) derives a no-arbitrage European option model, while MIT's [15.450 lecture notes](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/15-450-analytics-of-finance-fall-2010/pages/lecture-notes/) cover arbitrage-free pricing, simulation, and model extensions. A theoretical price is a model output, not an executable quote.

**Accounting gate:** For A/C, unit checks pass for long and short legs, multi-leg cash flows, expiry outcomes, and a corporate action. Portfolio P&L must reconcile to starting capital plus all cash flows and marked positions on every date. For B, reconcile published index levels, methodology, and comparator returns without implying a trade ledger was reconstructed.

### 4. Model fills and costs explicitly

Never assume every order fills at the midpoint. Start with a conservative, reproducible rule using contemporaneous NBBO and visible size. Model limit-order nonfills, partial fills, leg risk, bid/ask, broker and exchange fees, hedge turnover, market impact for larger size, and slippage in stressed periods. A multi-leg strategy must be executable as a package at the assumed price or simulated with the risk of legging. A signal formed at a bar's close cannot trade at that same close unless the information and order timing make that possible.

For A/C, run at least three execution cases: optimistic modeled assumption, base, and adverse. An assumed midpoint fill is optimistic; its live feasibility is not established by a displayed quote. Compare model fills with observed paper fills when available, but do not treat simulator fills as live execution evidence. Calibrate with actual live execution records if they later exist. For B, audit the published index's own hypothetical execution assumptions and do not substitute them for actual account fills. [Muravyev and Pearson](https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/33/11/4973/5732665) find that effective option spreads can be substantially below conventional quoted-spread estimates when traders time execution, while [de Silva, So, and Smith](https://academic.oup.com/rof/article-abstract/30/2/489/8301159) document large spreads and losses for retail option purchases around earnings announcements. Neither finding supplies a universal fill rate for this strategy; estimate its own costs.

**Execution gate:** For A, show that the program handles fills, nonfills, partial fills, and open exposure without claiming an edge. For B, explain the index methodology's costs and unknown live fill differences. For C, show net results under all three cases and the break-even extra slippage per contract. If a small fill adjustment erases a claimed result, label the hypothesis unproven.

### 5. Separate discovery from evaluation

Use chronological development, validation, and untouched final test periods where a genuinely unseen period can be reserved. Tune only on development data. Freeze rules before the final period. For repeated tuning or overlapping trades, use a walk-forward design with appropriate gaps or embargoes so one event does not leak into both training and testing. Level C reports results by market regime, underlying, expiration tenor, liquidity bucket, and calendar year. A reports synthetic case coverage and misses. B reports published index and comparator results by available periods and methodology regimes; a public history you already examined is descriptive, not an untouched confirmatory test. Include every failed trial in the experiment log; use multiple-testing controls or a backtest-overfitting estimate when searching many variants. A strategy that works only in one selected window has not passed.

**Validation gate:** Where a final segment was genuinely reserved, examine it once after the rules are frozen. Any subsequent change starts a new experiment with a new untouched period. For A, validate code on unseen synthetic cases. For B, state selection and methodology limits of the published series, especially if the entire public history was visible during selection. For C, report uncertainty intervals and the number of independent trades or events, not just the raw trade count; compare naive independent-trade inference with dependence-aware analysis on the portfolio series.

### 6. Compare against honest benchmarks

Choose the benchmark before seeing results. Depending on the exposure, compare with cash, the underlying total-return investment, a delta-matched position, a simple fixed-rule options strategy, or a public options index. Align starting capital, cash yield, financing, exposure, rebalance frequency, fees, and risk. The [Cboe BXM](https://www.cboe.com/us/indices/dashboard/bxm/) is a published S&P 500 covered-call benchmark; read its [current methodology](https://cdn.cboe.com/api/global/us_indices/governance/Cboe_BuyWrite_Indices_Methodology.pdf) and hypothetical-index assumptions before using it. For volatility-selling ideas, study the [variance risk premium](https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/22/3/1311/1581057) and ask whether the apparent reward compensates for crash and liquidity risk. Historical option premia can change: [Dew-Becker and Giglio](https://www.nber.org/papers/w31833) report that the variance risk premium narrowed toward zero in the last 15 years of their sample ending in 2022, so a past premium is not a permanent edge.

For C, report total **net** return, sample length, drawdown, volatility, tail loss, exposure, turnover, capacity, fee and slippage drag, and return relative to the benchmark. For B, report published-index return and drawdown under its methodology and state account-specific fees, slippage, and capacity as unknown unless independently measured. A reports simulator correctness and modeled costs only. Annualize returns only when the observation period and compounding assumptions make that informative; never present a short sample's annualized rate without its underlying dates and cash flows. Win rate and premium collected are supporting statistics, never primary outcomes.

### 7. Stress the entire portfolio

For A/C portfolios, aggregate positions by underlying, sector, expiry, and correlated risk factor. Record delta dollars, gamma, vega, theta, directional notional, worst contractual loss where defined, cash required after exercise or assignment, and margin utilization where known. Reprice the portfolio under joint shocks: gap up/down, volatility level and skew changes, time passage, correlation breakdown, widening spreads, and reduced liquidity. Test both historical episodes and invented scenarios more severe than the training sample. A spread's displayed expiration max loss does not describe every interim funding or execution problem. For B, report the published index's observed stress-period behavior and methodology assumptions; use a separately labeled hypothetical portfolio for cash/assignment practice. Do not infer actual constituent fills or account funding from index levels.

OCC's [STANS margin overview](https://www.theocc.com/risk-management/margin-methodology) uses portfolio simulation plus dependence and concentration stress components at the clearing-member level; it is a useful model for thinking in portfolio scenarios, though its margin is **not** a personal loss limit. [Cboe's stress-test description](https://www.cboe.com/solutions/options-analytics/portfolio-margin-analytics/stress-tests/) covers price, volatility, time, and historical-event shocks. [IBKR Risk Navigator lessons](https://www.interactivebrokers.com/campus/trading-course/ibkrs-risk-navigator/) demonstrate what-if portfolio and margin scenarios.

**Risk gate:** A/C publish the largest modeled loss and cash requirement for every portfolio scenario, the concentration map, and a written response if a limit is breached. B publishes index drawdown and stress-period sensitivity, the unknowns that published levels cannot reveal, and a separate hypothetical cash/assignment stress exercise. No position is justified by average return alone.

### 8. Forward-validate and audit

For C, run the frozen system in shadow mode using only information available at each decision time. Timestamp the signal, intended order, observed market, hypothetical or paper fill, rejection, and reason for every action. Compare opportunity frequency, spread, modeled fill rate, slippage, Greeks, and P&L with the research assumptions. Maintain a daily risk dashboard and monthly discrepancy review. Stop or redesign when data integrity fails, execution diverges materially, or drawdown breaches the prespecified research limit. For A, preserve unseen synthetic cases and regression results. For B, preserve new published index and comparator values with release dates and methodology notices. Do not quietly retune any evaluation rule while its designated forward record is being measured.

**Forward gate:** Level C presents a dated, complete decision log, including days with no trades and orders that did not fill, and explains material backtest-to-forward differences. Level B tracks newly published index values and methodology changes; level A adds unseen synthetic regression cases. Neither B nor A should present this as forward evidence for an executable edge. Moving to real capital is a separate personal decision and should never follow automatically from a paper result.

## Capstones

| Evidence level | Deliverable | Passing evidence and limit |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Simulator validation** | Synthetic contract and quote audit, special-event ledger, nonfill and adjustment cases, clean-run tests and reproducible manifest. | Another reviewer can reproduce code behavior on seen and unseen cases. No market edge is inferred. |
| **B. Published-index analysis** | Published index methodology, dated history, matched published comparator and sensitivity to stated index assumptions. | Source series and return differences reconcile. Missing option fills are stated, not invented. |
| **C. Historical contract replay** | Preregistered economic hypothesis, point-in-time contract selection, cost-aware ledger, one untouched final test, benchmark, multiple-testing, stress and forward reports. | An independent reviewer reproduces net results, exclusions, sensitivities, cash/share obligations and discrepancies. Historical and forward uncertainty remain explicit. |

The advanced track can extend to implied-volatility surface construction, stochastic-volatility models, and dynamic hedging after these capstones. MIT's [2024 mathematics-in-finance course](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-642-topics-in-mathematics-with-applications-in-finance-fall-2024/) provides problem sets and projects; [Gatheral and Jacquier](https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.0646) address arbitrage-free volatility surfaces. More complex modeling raises the standard of validation; it does not replace the data, execution, and risk gates above.

title: Options risk and operations curriculum
body:
# Options risk and operations curriculum

**Scope:** U.S. exchange-listed securities options. **Reviewed:** October 26, 2026. This is an educational curriculum and sample process, not a recommendation to open a position or a substitute for a broker's rules, the contract specifications, or individual tax advice. Recheck the linked primary sources and the broker's current procedures before live trading.

The course treats correct operations and survival as prerequisites for strategy research. A favorable payoff diagram does not remove execution, assignment, settlement, liquidity, tax, or broker risks.

## Required reading and knowledge checks

| Reading | What the learner must be able to explain |
| --- | --- |
| [OCC *Characteristics and Risks of Standardized Options* (ODD)](https://www.theocc.com/company-information/documents-and-archives/options-disclosure-document) | Rights versus obligations; exercise and assignment; risks of buyers, writers, and combinations; adjusted contracts. OCC says investors must read the ODD before buying or selling options. |
| [SEC: An Introduction to Options](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-63) | Premium, strike, expiration, multiplier, payoff, and why a buyer can lose the entire premium while certain writers can lose more than the initial investment. |
| [SEC: Opening an Options Account](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-77) and [FINRA Rule 2360](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/rulebooks/finra-rules/2360) | Broker approval comes before options orders; permissions depend on experience, objectives, finances, and the broker's approval scheme. Levels and allowed strategies vary by firm. Do not misstate experience or finances to obtain approval. |
| [OIC: Exercising Options](https://www.optionseducation.org/optionsoverview/exercising-options) and [OIC: Assignment FAQ](https://www.optionseducation.org/referencelibrary/faq/options-assignment) | An American-style short option may be assigned on any business day, including before expiration. Explain ex-dividend and deep-in-the-money cases, and why a short in-the-money option should generally be expected to be assigned at expiration. |
| [FINRA: Understanding Assignment](https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/trading-options-understanding-assignment) | Assignment of one leg can leave stock and a surviving option. A spread's long option is not automatically exercised to resolve the obligation. After-hours moves can change exercise decisions after the regular close. |
| [SEC: Understanding Margin Accounts](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-29) | Margin interest, calls and liquidation, and why some short-option strategies can create losses greater than the initial investment. |
| [Cboe S&P 500 product comparison](https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/sp_500/spx_weekly_options/specifications) | Verify each contract's underlying, multiplier, exercise style, cash versus physical settlement, and A.M. versus P.M. settlement. Cboe lists SPX/SPXW/XSP as European-style and cash-settled, versus SPY ETF options as American-style and physically settled. |
| [IRS Publication 550](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p550) and [Form 6781](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-6781) | Keep complete tax records. The linked Publication 550 is the 2025 edition as of this review; check the relevant tax-year instructions before filing. Some qualifying broad-based index options may be Section 1256 contracts, generally subject to year-end mark-to-market and 60/40 capital-gain treatment; equity options, covered calls, straddles, and hedges can follow other rules. Determine actual treatment with a qualified tax professional. |

**Assessment:** The learner must calculate cash flows and worst-case obligations without looking up a payoff chart, and must find the primary contract specification and broker exercise instructions for a product. Passing a multiple-choice quiz alone is insufficient. Work the complete, fictional account ledgers and fresh cases in [OPERATIONAL_CASEBOOK.md](OPERATIONAL_CASEBOOK.md); the solution section is for checking a finished attempt.

## Risk scenarios to rehearse before any live order

1. **Long call expires worthless.** Calculate total cash lost, including fees, and explain why “cheap premium” does not make a high-probability trade. The [SEC options bulletin](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-63) states buyers can lose the full premium.
2. **Uncovered short call gaps upward.** Show the obligation to deliver shares and why the loss has no fixed theoretical ceiling. No learner may practice this with a live order under the sample policy. See the [SEC leverage bulletin](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins/leveraged-investing-strategies-know-risks-using-these-advanced-investment-tools).
3. **Short call on a dividend-paying stock approaches an ex-dividend date.** Determine whether early exercise is plausible and whether a buy-to-close order can be filled before that day's option market close. A broker's exercise cutoff applies to a holder's exercise instructions; it is not a guaranteed exit window for a short position. [OIC](https://www.optionseducation.org/optionsoverview/exercising-options) says dividend dates can increase early-call assignment risk and that an open short can be assigned before expiration.
4. **Short leg of a vertical is assigned.** Recompute stock position, cash/share requirement, margin need, remaining option exposure, and exit choices. The apparent maximum loss shown for the *intact* spread is not a guarantee once the legs separate or the underlying moves after hours. Work through [FINRA's examples](https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/trading-options-understanding-assignment).
5. **Expiration close differs from after-hours market.** Model a short option that looked out of the money at the close but was exercised following an after-hours price move. Learn broker-specific exercise and do-not-exercise deadlines. See [OIC assignment guidance](https://www.optionseducation.org/referencelibrary/faq/options-assignment) and [FINRA's spread example](https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/trading-options-understanding-assignment).
6. **A.M. versus P.M. index settlement.** Retrieve the exchange specifications for a proposed expiry and calculate settlement cash, including the effect of a gap between last trading time and the settlement value. Start with [Cboe's specifications](https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/sp_500/spx_weekly_options/specifications).
7. **Liquidity shock.** Reprice an exit at the bid for a long option or ask for a short option, then widen the spread and include fees. A model mid-price is not a guaranteed fill. State when the plan requires no trade.
8. **Broker intervention.** Explain how a margin deficit or insufficient shares/cash may lead to rejected orders or forced liquidation, and how such action could differ from the planned exit. Review the [SEC margin bulletin](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-29) and the broker's agreement.

## Account and rule check before live trading

- Record the **broker and account type**, approved strategies, option buying power, margin agreement, house requirements, fees, and whether complex orders can be entered and closed as a package. Broker approval levels are not standardized: [SEC](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-77).
- Obtain the broker's **exercise, do-not-exercise, and expiration liquidation deadlines** in the account's time zone. Confirm how instructions are submitted and what happens if cash or shares are insufficient. Do not assume the exchange close is the broker's cutoff: [OIC](https://www.optionseducation.org/optionsoverview/exercising-options).
- Check the exact **underlying, deliverable, contract multiplier, exercise style, settlement type/value, expiration, last trading time, and corporate-action adjustment** for each series. Do not infer SPX rules from SPY, or one expiration's settlement from another's: [Cboe](https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/sp_500/spx_weekly_options/specifications), [OCC ODD](https://www.theocc.com/company-information/documents-and-archives/options-disclosure-document).
- Confirm **current day-trading and margin treatment with the broker**. FINRA replaced its pattern-day-trader day-trade-count and $25,000 minimum-equity framework with new intraday margin standards effective June 4, 2026. Member firms may phase in implementation through October 20, 2027, and can impose stricter house requirements. The new rule does not make margin risk-free; FINRA notes a $2,000 minimum equity to use leverage and an intraday maintenance-margin framework. Do not present either the old $25,000 threshold or a particular broker's implementation as universal. [FINRA Notice 26-10](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/notices/26-10); [FINRA investor explanation](https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/intraday-margin-requirements).
- Build a tax ledger recording trade and exercise dates, contract identifiers, fees, premiums, assignments, underlying share basis, and year-end open positions. Review [IRS Publication 550](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p550) and [Form 6781 guidance](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-6781); obtain individual tax advice before relying on a particular treatment.

## Training gates

These are curriculum standards, not regulator requirements or proof of profitability. Failure means repeat the relevant module before advancing within this optional extended training policy. The [beginner microcourse](beginner/README.md) stands on its own: quantitative programming, a 104-week schedule, and a research capstone are not prerequisites for beginning, understanding a personal decision, or choosing not to trade. No course grade automatically approves live trading.

### Gate 1 — Market and contract literacy

- Complete the readings above and score at least **90%** on an independently written concept exam.
- Correctly draw and calculate expiration payoff, maximum *modeled* loss, break-even, and stock/cash obligation for long calls/puts, covered calls, cash-secured puts, and vertical debit/credit spreads.
- Pass **all** of the assignment, settlement, after-hours, and broker-cutoff scenarios above, using the [casebook](OPERATIONAL_CASEBOOK.md) to show before/after positions and cash. Every wrong operational answer is remediated and retested on a fresh case.

### Gate 2 — Simulated orders and risk process

- For at least **8 weeks**, record decisions in a paper journal, including decisions *not* to trade. Module 12 starts this record in weeks 45–48; continue it through at least weeks 49–52 while studying probability, and longer if the gate remains incomplete. Include at least **30 complete decision records** spanning quiet, volatile, and event-driven sessions; do not manufacture activity to satisfy a quota.
- Each simulated order has a written thesis, entry and exit condition, explicit worst-case obligation, position size, underlying event calendar, bid/ask spread, commissions, and a plausible adverse fill. Reconcile a sample of paper fills against quotes; paper platforms can give unrealistic fills.
- Run a documented stress test covering an overnight gap, volatility jump/crush, widening spreads, one-leg assignment, and a broker liquidation. Record the largest *modeled* cash/share obligation in each case; label any exposure without a finite theoretical ceiling.
- Show **100% adherence** to a written risk policy during the final four weeks. Complete the [quote and order-status replay](EXECUTION_PRACTICE.md), including nonfills and a cancellation that has not been confirmed. Profit in a simulator is neither required nor sufficient to pass; process and understanding are the gate.

### Gate 3 — Limited live practice, if financially appropriate

- Under this **optional advanced training policy**, live practice comes only after its Gates A–D in [COURSE.md](COURSE.md) and Gates 1–2 above. That is a conservative curriculum choice for this extended path, not a universal or regulatory requirement that every personal investor complete quantitative research. A separate personal decision still requires understanding the intended position, affordable losses, all share/cash obligations, the current ODD, broker permissions and procedures, and relevant account/tax circumstances. A synthetic software capstone alone supplies no real-market strategy evidence; claims about an edge need suitable real-market evidence, realistic execution assumptions, and forward observations. Completing either course does not certify live readiness, and remaining in observation or simulation is a valid outcome.
- Begin with a single small, fully paid, defined-risk position whose **contract-level** loss fits the written cash risk limit. If a single contract is too large, do not place a trade. Do not use margin borrowing, uncovered short options, or 0DTE as a shortcut to meet a sizing target.
- Record real fills, fees, execution delay, mistakes, and weekly account reconciliation. Increase size only after a separate review of sufficient live observations and risk-control adherence; a profitable week is not a sizing signal.

## Sample conservative training policy

**This is an illustrative classroom policy, not a claim that these thresholds are universally safe or optimal.** A learner may choose stricter limits, and anyone unable to lose the stated amount should not trade live.

| Rule | Sample limit or action |
| --- | --- |
| Capital | Use only money set aside for practice whose full loss would not disrupt living expenses or long-term obligations. No borrowing to fund the account. |
| Allowed initial positions | Fully paid long options or broker-approved defined-risk spreads only after the relevant strategy exam. Do not open uncovered short options. Prefer avoiding positions that could create unwanted shares. For American-style spreads, plan an exit before expiry, while recognizing that early assignment remains possible on any day the short leg is open. |
| Maximum new-position loss | At most **0.25% of practice account equity**. Calculate full premium or intact-spread theoretical maximum loss **plus entry, exit, and other expected fees per contract**. Choose the largest **whole-number quantity that remains within** the budget; never round the contract quantity up. Model additional assignment, slippage, and gap risks separately. No trade if one contract exceeds the limit. |
| Aggregate open-position modeled loss | At most **1% of practice account equity**, including correlated positions. Add stress scenarios; the modeled sum can underestimate real losses. |
| Loss pause | Stop placing new risk orders after a **1% decline in daily account equity**, **3% in weekly account equity**, or **5% from the cash-flow-adjusted equity high-water mark**. Include realized and open-position P&L; adjust for deposits and withdrawals, define the start/end times and marking rule, and flag stale marks. On a trigger, inspect actual positions and pending orders, cancel confirmed unnecessary entries, and follow the written plan to reduce or manage existing risk. Do not assume a submitted cancellation has succeeded. Resume only after a written review and a new plan. These are illustrative thresholds. |
| Execution | Use limit orders; specify the most adverse acceptable fill in advance. Cancel an order when the quote or thesis changes. Never treat a stop order as guaranteed protection against gaps. |
| Expiration and events | Check dividend, earnings, distribution, corporate-action, and last-trading/settlement calendars. Close or otherwise deliberately manage physical-settlement short legs before the last tradable time and any earlier broker risk-liquidation deadline. A buy-to-close order must fill to remove assignment exposure. |
| Advanced strategies | Margin leverage, uncovered options, complex ratio positions, and 0DTE require separate advanced study and a new risk policy. They are never prerequisites for mastery. |

For a paid option, initial modeled loss is premium × the actual contract multiplier + fees. For a standard one-to-one vertical credit spread with matching expiration, multiplier, and deliverable, the intact position's modeled maximum loss at expiration is (strike width − credit received) × the multiplier + fees. This formula **does not** capture every operational or post-expiration scenario and may not apply to adjusted contracts. Verify the series' deliverables before calculating risk. See the [OCC ODD](https://www.theocc.com/company-information/documents-and-archives/options-disclosure-document) and [FINRA assignment examples](https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/trading-options-understanding-assignment).

For example, a hypothetical $100,000 practice account has a $250 new-position budget under the 0.25% illustration. If one fully paid contract has $120 premium at risk and $2 total fees, the greatest permitted quantity by this rule is `floor(250 / 122) = 2`; two use $244, while three use $366. If the per-contract modeled loss is $260, the permitted quantity is zero. Separate share-delivery and liquidity stresses can still reject a position that fits this arithmetic.

**Equity and pause calculation:** Save account equity at a fixed daily and weekly start time, then calculate change as `current equity − starting equity − net external deposits` (a withdrawal is a negative deposit). Equity includes cash plus marked open positions and liabilities. State the valuation source; for a hypothetical liquidation view, mark long options at a plausible bid and short options at a plausible ask, then stress wider quotes. Keep a separate cash-flow-adjusted equity path for the high-water comparison. A $10,000 account with no deposits and $100 of open losses has fallen 1% even if no loss was realized. If quotes are stale or unavailable, record the uncertainty and use the contingency process instead of silently declaring the threshold unbreached. This illustration is a training rule, not a claim that every account should use these percentages.

## Reusable templates

### Pre-order card

```text
Date/time and account:
Underlying / exact option symbols / expirations:
Exchange contract specification link; multiplier and deliverable:
Exercise style; cash or physical settlement; A.M./P.M. value:
Event, dividend, earnings, and corporate-action checks:
Why this position? What observation would disprove the thesis?
Entry limit, current bid/ask, expected fees, adverse-fill assumption:
Planned exit or expiration action; broker cutoff:
Maximum modeled loss; gap/assignment/stock/cash stress case:
Account equity; position and aggregate risk after entry; whole-number size calculation:
Can I fund all possible share/cash obligations? If no, how will I avoid them?
Decision: enter / wait / abstain; reason:
```

### End-of-day and expiration check

```text
All positions and orders reconciled with broker statement? Yes/No
Any short American-style options with assignment risk? Which?
Any ex-dividend, earnings, split, merger, halt, or distribution tomorrow?
Any expiring options? Broker cutoff and exercise instructions recorded?
Any physical-delivery exposure requiring shares or cash?
Any spread whose legs could separate? Action and deadline?
Account equity including open marks, external cash flows, buying power, margin status, and loss-pause status:
Any order pending cancellation or unconfirmed status? Order IDs and resolution:
Trade journal complete; discrepancy escalated to broker if needed?
```

### Weekly risk review

```text
Starting/ending cash-flow-adjusted equity; realized and unrealized P&L; fees and slippage:
Largest position and aggregate modeled loss; peak-to-trough decline:
Number of rule violations and near misses (target: zero):
Assignment/settlement/corporate-action surprises:
Paper versus executable-fill differences:
What evidence supports or weakens each trading hypothesis?
Next week's size: same / lower / no live trading, with reason:
```

## Maintenance rule

Review OCC disclosures, exchange specifications, FINRA margin rules, broker procedures, and IRS guidance at least annually and whenever a product, broker, strategy, or tax year changes. Date each review in the trading journal. The 2026 FINRA intraday-margin transition makes broker-specific verification especially important through October 2027.

title: Options trading course: source library
body:
# Options trading course: source library

Reviewed October 26, 2026. This is a curated reading and practice list for the course, not a claim to cover every course, blog, or book online. Start with the free resources. Paid texts and historical option data are optional until the learner reaches the research stages. Prices, access terms, broker procedures, and rules can change; verify them at the linked source when used.

## How sources were selected

1. **Mechanics and risk:** Prefer the SEC, OCC, FINRA, exchanges, and original product specifications over influencer summaries.
2. **Learning:** Prefer coherent lessons with exercises, quizzes, or simulations. A strategy description alone does not establish that it makes money.
3. **Research:** Prefer original academic papers and datasets with documented fields, timestamps, adjustment rules, and licensing.
4. **Claims about performance:** Require executable assumptions, bid/ask and fees, out-of-sample tests, and drawdowns. Treat testimonials, win rates, and backtests without these as ideas to test.
5. **Current details:** Recheck disclosure documents, margin and broker policies, product settlement, and data specifications before live use. Historical textbooks explain models, not current brokerage rules.

## Practice supplied with this course

Use the [math bridge](FOUNDATION_MATH_BRIDGE.md) and [separate assessment and answer files](FOUNDATION_ASSESSMENTS.md) before buying another introductory course. The [operational casebook](OPERATIONAL_CASEBOOK.md) supplies account and assignment scenarios; [execution practice](EXECUTION_PRACTICE.md) supplies timestamped order decisions; the [dynamic hedging lab](DYNAMIC_HEDGING_LAB.md) reconciles an option and stock hedge. The [Python labs](labs/README.md) provide small **synthetic** data and runnable accounting, data-quality, execution, and research checks. Synthetic data test your process and software; they cannot establish a live trading edge. Record first attempts and corrections in [the learning record](LEARNING_RECORD_TEMPLATE.md).

Before acquiring historical option quotes, complete the feasibility screen in [the research lab](RESEARCH_LAB.md): exact contract universe, fields, timestamps, corporate-action treatment, license, cost, and the study that the data can support. Published index history, a delayed chain, and licensed contract-level quotes answer different questions. The [three later paths](MASTERY_TRACKS.md) set different project standards for personal portfolio decisions, independent research, and professional preparation.

## Required free starting set

| Source | What it contributes | Course use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [SEC: An Introduction to Options](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-63) | Plain-language listed stock option terms and the possibility of losing all premium or more. Updated July 16, 2026. | First reading; explain a call, put, strike, expiration, contract multiplier, and buyer/writer obligation in your own words. |
| [SEC: Opening an Options Account](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-77) | Broker approval, disclosures, and trading levels. Updated July 16, 2026. | Understand why account approval and permissions differ by broker and strategy. |
| [OCC: Characteristics and Risks of Standardized Options](https://www.theocc.com/company-information/documents-and-archives/options-disclosure-document) | The official options disclosure document (ODD). OCC identifies the June 2024 edition as the current full document on this page. | Required reference before any live options trading; revisit chapters for each new strategy or product. |
| [OIC/OCC Learning: Options Academy](https://prd-web.optionseducation.org/theoptionseducationcenter/occ-learning) | Free, self-paced sequence covering Options 101, exercise/assignment, Greeks, historical versus implied volatility, and selling strategies, with quizzes. | Main beginner course; complete quizzes and summarize each strategy's obligation and worst plausible exposure. |
| [Cboe Options Institute](https://www.cboe.com/optionsinstitute) and [Learning Portal](https://www.cboe.com/optionsinstitute/learningportal/) | Public Options 101, calls, puts, market mechanics, plus free portal learning paths, classes, and webinar replays. | Alternate explanations and later modules on index options, spreads, hedging, and portfolio risk. Portal may require registration. |
| [IBKR Campus: Options](https://www.interactivebrokers.com/campus/traders-academy/options/) and [course catalog](https://www.interactivebrokers.com/campus/traders-academy/finance-courses/) | Free lessons and quizzes. IBKR's stated sequence is Options Essentials → Introduction to Options → Basic Hedging → Basic Option Strategies → TWS Option Tools → Neutral Option Strategies → Advanced Option Strategies → Interactive Learning – Options Education. | Second explanation and platform mechanics; distinguish educational concepts from broker-specific buttons and permissions. |
| [FINRA: Understanding Assignment](https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/trading-options-understanding-assignment) | Short-option obligations, early assignment, and the risk that one leg of a spread is assigned. | Required case study before studying short options or spreads. |

## Practice tools and adjacent markets

| Source | What it contributes | Use and limitation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [OIC quotes and calculators](https://prd-web.optionseducation.org/options-quotes-calculators) | Option chain, pricing, probability, and historical/implied volatility tools. | Explore inputs and contract details. Market data is delayed about 20 minutes; do not treat the quotes as executable live prices or a historical backtest database. |
| [OIC profit and loss simulator](https://www.optionseducation.org/oic-profit-and-loss-simulator) | Scenario analysis for single- and multi-leg positions, including price, time, volatility, and Greeks. | Build hypothetical profit-and-loss scenarios; rehearse exercise and assignment separately from the contract rules. Theoretical projections can differ from fills and future market prices. |
| [Cboe Options Institute tools](https://www.cboe.com/optionsinstitute/tools/trade-optimizer/) | Calculator and trade optimizer. | Compare candidate position structures and ask which market view each one actually expresses. |
| [IBKR: Options Strategy Research & Backtesting with ORATS](https://www.interactivebrokers.com/campus/trading-course/options-strategy-research-and-backtesting-with-orats/) | A course on historical strategy tests, return, win rate, drawdown, strikes, expiry, and volatility. | Introduction to research workflows; independently audit data, assumptions, fees, and test selection. Access to the ORATS tool may depend on account or subscriptions. |
| [IBKR: Paper Trading Account](https://www.interactivebrokers.com/campus/trading-lessons/how-to-open-an-ibkr-paper-trading-account/) | Broker paper-account setup. | The [current account guide](https://www.ibkrguides.com/orgportal/aboutpapertradingaccount.htm), checked November 14, 2026, says its regular paper account requires an existing funded account and separately offers a Free Trial for exploring before funding. A written shadow ledger also works; no account funding is needed for this course. Simulated fills are not evidence of a live trading edge. |
| [IBKR: Paper Trading Limitations](https://www.ibkrguides.com/orgportal/aboutpapertradingaccount.htm) | Broker documentation of simulated fills, limited combo trading, and unsupported order types. | Compare simulator behavior with real quote-side execution assumptions before interpreting paper results. |
| [CME: Introduction to Options](https://www.cmegroup.com/education/courses/introduction-to-options) and [All About Options](https://www.cmegroup.com/education/courses/curriculum-all-about-options) | Options-on-futures education. The course page did not expose a lesson catalog in the November 14, 2026 public-text check, so no current lesson count is asserted. | Later specialization after equity and index option mechanics. Confirm current catalog and access at CME; futures-option underlyings, multipliers, margin, and settlement need separate study. |
| [CME Trading Simulator](https://www.cmegroup.com/articles/faqs/trading-simulator-faq.html) | Free simulator with CME futures and options on futures. Practice-mode market data is delayed 10 minutes. | Practice futures-option order flow, not equity options. CME says the simulator does not automatically handle open positions at expiry, so close positions before expiry in the simulator. |

## Formal finance and advanced options study

These are sequenced after the learner can derive option payoffs, explain assignment, and calculate basic position risk.

| Source | What it contributes | Access |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [MIT OpenCourseWare: Finance Theory I, options lectures](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/15-401-finance-theory-i-fall-2008/pages/video-lectures-and-slides/options/) | Free videos/slides on options, payoff diagrams, volatility bets, and the binomial pricing model. The [full course](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/15-401-finance-theory-i-fall-2008/) also covers fixed income, portfolio theory, and efficient markets. | Free. A sound bridge from market vocabulary to valuation. |
| [Khan Academy: Algebra Basics](https://www.khanacademy.org/mission/algebra-basics) and [Statistics and Probability](https://www.khanacademy.org/math/statistics-probability) | Free courses with exercises and unit tests for learners who need a math bridge. | Start here if algebra, functions, or elementary statistics are unfamiliar; extend the course timeline as needed. |
| [MIT OpenCourseWare: Single Variable Calculus](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-01sc-single-variable-calculus-fall-2010/) and [Introduction to Probability and Statistics](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-05-introduction-to-probability-and-statistics-spring-2022/pages/syllabus/) | Free mathematical courses with practice problems and solutions. MIT 18.05 formally lists multivariable calculus as a prerequisite. | Study calculus before attempting the full MIT 18.05 problem sets; use Khan Academy for the beginner statistics sequence. |
| [MIT OpenCourseWare: Introduction to CS and Programming Using Python](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-100l-introduction-to-cs-and-programming-using-python-fall-2022/) and [Python's official tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/) | MIT 6.100L is designed for people with little or no programming experience; Python's own tutorial assumes prior programming knowledge. | Begin with MIT if new to coding, then use the official tutorial as a language reference; save runnable scripts and inputs. |
| [MIT OpenCourseWare: Analytics of Finance](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/15-450-analytics-of-finance-fall-2010/pages/lecture-notes/) | Arbitrage-free pricing, stochastic calculus, Monte Carlo, estimation, statistical tests, and volatility models, with code and problem sets. Its [syllabus](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/15-450-analytics-of-finance-fall-2010/pages/syllabus/) assumes calculus, probability, statistics, and programming. | Free; advanced quantitative track. |
| [MIT OpenCourseWare: Mathematics with Applications in Finance (2024)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-642-topics-in-mathematics-with-applications-in-finance-fall-2024/) | Modern lecture and project track connecting mathematics, pricing, and risk. | Free advanced extension after the core pricing module. |
| [John C. Hull, *Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives*, 11th ed.](https://www.pearson.com/en-us/subject-catalog/p/options-futures-and-other-derivatives/P200000005938/9780136939979) | Broad derivatives theory: forwards/futures, options, no-arbitrage pricing, hedging, and model foundations. | Paid Pearson text; borrow from a library if possible. |
| [Sheldon Natenberg, *Option Volatility and Pricing*, 2nd ed.](https://www.mheducation.com/highered/mhp/product/option-volatility-pricing-advanced-trading-strategies-techniques-2nd-edition.html) | Trader-oriented volatility, dynamic hedging, risk analysis, spreads, and position management. | Paid McGraw Hill text; use once Greeks and parity are comfortable. |
| [Euan Sinclair, *Volatility Trading*, 2nd ed.](https://www.wiley.com/en-us/-p-9781118416723) | Volatility measurement, hedging, sizing, trade evaluation, and the variance premium. | Paid Wiley text; use for research and portfolio design, not as a source of automatic trade signals. |

## Data and primary research for the advanced stage

| Source | Research use and caveat |
| --- | --- |
| [Cboe historical VIX and volatility indices](https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/vix_historical_data) | Free daily index history for volatility context. VIX is an index, not a complete history of executable option quotes. |
| [OCC volume query](https://www.theocc.com/market-data/market-data-reports/volume-and-open-interest/volume-query), [open-interest reports](https://www.theocc.com/market-data/market-data-reports/volume-and-open-interest/open-interest), and [information memos](https://infomemo.theocc.com/infomemo/search-memo) | Official options volume and open-interest reports; memos document contract adjustments and special deliverables after corporate actions. Confirm each report's available date range before designing a study. |
| [SEC EDGAR filings](https://www.sec.gov/search-filings) | Free issuer filings for earnings and corporate-event research; record the filing timestamp to avoid look-ahead bias. |
| [FRED SOFR](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SOFR) and [3-month Treasury yield](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS3MO) | Public interest-rate series. Align publication and observation dates with the simulated decision time; cite source and transformations. |
| [Cboe DataShop option quote intervals](https://datashop.cboe.com/option-quote-intervals) | Historical NBBO bid/ask, sizes, volume, and optional Greeks for U.S. listed equity, ETF, and index options. This is a paid dataset; confirm exact fields, timestamps, coverage, licensing, and costs before buying. It does not cover options on futures. Cboe says its quote-size capture changed on June 22, 2026, which matters for historical liquidity comparisons. |
| [OptionMetrics IvyDB US](https://optionmetrics.com/united-states/) | Research-grade daily option bids/asks, volume, open interest, Greeks, volatility surfaces, and corporate-action handling. Commercial/institutional access; inspect methodology and survivorship coverage. |
| [Bakshi and Kapadia, 2003, *Delta-Hedged Gains and the Negative Market Volatility Risk Premium*](https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/16/2/527/1579962) | Original empirical study connecting delta-hedged option returns and volatility risk. Historical finding to replicate and stress-test, not a current trade recommendation. |
| [Tian and Wu, 2023, *Limits of Arbitrage and Primary Risk-Taking in Derivative Securities*](https://academic.oup.com/raps/article-abstract/13/3/405/7035950) | Delta hedging reduces, but does not eliminate, risk; useful for decomposing the risks left in an options strategy. |
| [Bailey et al., *The Probability of Backtest Overfitting*](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2326253) | Original research on strategy selection bias and why repeated backtest searches can produce fragile winners. Use to design a fixed test protocol and holdout evaluation. |

## Review cadence

Check SEC, FINRA, OCC, exchange product specifications, broker permissions, and data-vendor documentation before every new live-product module. In particular, [FINRA's 2026 intraday margin transition guidance](https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/intraday-margin-requirements) says firms may remain on older day-trading requirements during the transition through October 20, 2027; confirm the rule actually applied by the learner's broker. Review this source library at least quarterly and record newly verified dates and replacement links.

## Verification boundary

The public source descriptions and links above were rechecked on October 26, 2026. This review did not log into the Cboe learning portal or a broker, execute a simulator order, or purchase a historical data product. Tool features, course access, historical coverage, and trade fills should be confirmed inside the relevant account before relying on them. Some publisher and academic pages restrict automated access; their bibliographic details were cross-checked against the publisher's or journal's indexed page.

title: Your first options course session
body:
# Your first options course session

**Today takes 10–15 minutes. You do not need to know anything about trading.** Your only task is [Lesson 01 in Money and markets](beginner/01_MARKETS.md).

Read **only Lesson 01**. Its idea is that your first goal is understanding. Work through its example, write your own answer to its one question, then open the answer. You may stop there.

## Your daily routine

| Minutes | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| 0–2 | Recall yesterday's one idea without looking. On your first day, write why you want to learn. |
| 2–8 | Read one lesson and follow its worked example. |
| 8–12 | Answer the new question before revealing the solution. |
| 12–15 | Correct one mistake and write the idea in your own words. |

Some lessons need two sessions. This is expected. There is no deadline and no requirement to trade.

## A glimpse of Lesson 02

A **share** is a small ownership interest in a company. If you buy two shares at $10 each, the shares cost $20 before fees. If their market price later falls to $8 each, they are worth $16 together. The price can move in either direction. This ownership idea comes before learning the contracts called options. [The SEC explains stocks](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/investment-products/stocks).

You do not have to study calls, puts, Greeks or strategies today. Those arrive in small steps after the basic market lessons.

**Continue:** [Lesson 01](beginner/01_MARKETS.md) · [Course map](beginner/README.md) · [How to study](HOW_TO_STUDY.md)

For guided teaching in chat, say **“Teach me Lesson 1. One idea at a time, and wait for my answer.”** The app and the course files contain the full teaching material if you prefer to work independently.

The older intensive introduction is preserved as [Advanced first week](ADVANCED_FIRST_WEEK.md) for learners following the optional long curriculum.

title: Ready for external review and learner participation
body:
# Ready for external review and learner participation

Prepared November 14, 2026. The owner selected **prepare the materials; participants will come later**. No participant is enrolled and no approval is recorded on the owner's behalf.

## Work completed now

- [Technical audit and remediation record](COURSE_TECHNICAL_AUDIT.md): 3,724 independent numerical assertions, review of all 26 advanced cases, and an audit of assessment/review integrity. All reported findings were corrected and verified. This is an AI-assisted technical review, not a human expert endorsement.
- [External review packet](EXTERNAL_REVIEW_PACKET.md): review scope, qualification and independence declarations, coverage checklist, anchored 0–3 rubric, two-reviewer calibration, discrepancy log and unfilled approval fields.
- [Parallel written cases](PILOT_PARALLEL_CASES.md): four fictional forms with different cash, share-retention, partial-fill and adjusted-deliverable conditions. Eight learner files separate initial packets from updates; the participant ZIP contains no instructor keys. All 80 wealth-table cells and five residual-position states were checked independently.
- [Rating and report template](PILOT_RATING_AND_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md): actual prior knowledge, exposure, consent, assistance, confidence, elapsed time, paired ratings, missing follow-ups and a report structure. Outcome and sign-off fields remain blank.

## Materials in the private course

Open **Advanced academy → Teaching studio → Learning pilot** for the downloads:

- Learner packets without keys: `pilot-participant-forms.zip`.
- Review and rating guide: `validation-guide.md`.
- Complete facilitator course, original case blueprints and instructor keys: `options-course.zip`.

The Resource library also includes every review/pilot document and this readiness record. A knowledgeable facilitator should adapt and recheck a form before describing it as unfamiliar. A public blueprint or a case whose solution has been read is practice material rather than an unseen assessment.

## Evidence controls verified

The advanced review scale is consistently 0–3. All actual ratings remain in the history; the calibration view compares distinct named external reviewers' reported ratings and excludes self-review. Reviewer identity and independence are attributed, not independently authenticated by the application.

New numerical pilots record explicit consent, prior experience and observed prior course activity. Results retain self-reported confidence and assistance alongside time and clarity. The blueprint version and fingerprint cover form wording, units, expected results, explanations and numerical grading tolerances. Unsupported or changed blueprints cannot silently replace a longitudinal assessment. Follow-up windows use server time; absent visits stay absent.

## Actual participation deferred by the owner

A read-only inspection of the live database found zero advanced submissions, zero advanced practice sets and zero teaching events on November 14, 2026. There was no existing learner work or expert judgment to evaluate. Local software tests use temporary fixtures and restore the test records; their scores are not participant outcomes.

When participants are available, use the prepared protocol to obtain agreement, preserve a genuine baseline, administer teaching and transfer forms, collect actual follow-ups and obtain real qualified reviewers' assessments. Those activities remain deferred until the owner supplies participants. No finding here claims MBA accreditation or proven teaching effectiveness.

title: Independent verification of the options course
body:
# Independent verification of the options course

**Checked:** October 26, 2026. **Scope:** [README.md](README.md), [START_HERE.md](START_HERE.md), [COURSE.md](COURSE.md), [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md), [RISK_AND_OPERATIONS.md](RISK_AND_OPERATIONS.md), and [RESEARCH_LAB.md](RESEARCH_LAB.md). This report records a second review of factual claims, source fit, worked arithmetic, and internal consistency. The 104-week schedule and grading thresholds are curriculum design choices, not empirically proven routes to elite performance.

## Verification method

We re-read the materials against current pages from the SEC, OCC/OIC, FINRA, Cboe, CME, IBKR, IRS, MIT, the relevant publishers and data vendors, and the abstracts or texts of cited original research. We checked the option payoff calculations independently, mapped the curriculum's prerequisites, and verified all Markdown file references. The project has 70 distinct external URLs across the six original documents and 14 internal document links; all 14 internal links resolve. Public source descriptions were checked against their providers. Account-only features and licensed historical data were not represented as directly tested.

## What the second review found

| Area | Verification result and correction |
| --- | --- |
| Beginner contract description | The initial lesson described share delivery too broadly. It now says its examples are **standard physically settled stock options**. [OIC distinguishes these from cash-settled index options](https://www.optionseducation.org/advancedconcepts/equity-vs-index-options); the [OCC disclosure document](https://www.theocc.com/company-information/documents-and-archives/options-disclosure-document) also distinguishes physical delivery and cash settlement. |
| Worked arithmetic | Recomputed the $105 call bought for $3: at a $112 stock price on expiration its net payoff is `(112 − 105) × 100 − 300 = $400`; at $106 it is `−$200`; break-even is $108. Recomputed the $95 put bought for $2: at $88 it returns `$500` after premium, and break-even is $93. A $2.10/$2.30 quote costs $20 for a one-contract immediate ask-to-bid round trip before fees. The seven-day plan totals 10 hours; 104 weeks × 10 hours is 1,040 hours. These are classroom expiration/payoff examples, not guaranteed broker outcomes. |
| Curriculum sequence | Same-expiration payoff exercises no longer include calendars: a calendar retains a live leg when the near leg expires. Calendars now appear after Greeks and term structure. The safety sprint now explicitly uses eight sourced scenarios plus two learner-generated cases. |
| Math prerequisites | [MIT 18.05](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-05-introduction-to-probability-and-statistics-spring-2022/pages/syllabus/) formally requires multivariable calculus. The course now starts beginner statistics with [Khan Academy](https://www.khanacademy.org/math/statistics-probability), with MIT as a later extension. The 104-week target extends if foundational math needs work. |
| Coding prerequisites | [Python's official tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/) explicitly addresses people who already know programming. The course now starts non-programmers with [MIT 6.100L](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-100l-introduction-to-cs-and-programming-using-python-fall-2022/). |
| Account, assignment, and settlement | The [SEC account bulletin](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins-77) supports broker-specific approval. [OIC](https://www.optionseducation.org/optionsoverview/exercising-options) and [FINRA](https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/trading-options-understanding-assignment) support early assignment and a spread leg leaving stock exposure. The risk guide now distinguishes a short seller's last chance to **buy to close** from a long holder's broker exercise cutoff, states that a close order must fill, and limits the vertical credit-spread formula to matching standard one-to-one contracts. [Cboe specifications](https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/sp_500/spx_weekly_options/specifications) confirm the SPX/SPXW/XSP versus SPY exercise and settlement distinctions used in the course. |
| 2026 margin and tax | [FINRA Notice 26-10](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/notices/26-10) confirms the intraday margin change effective June 4, 2026 and broker phase-in through October 20, 2027; a universal $25,000 pattern-day-trader statement would be misleading during the transition. The risk guide requires broker verification. [IRS Publication 550](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p550) is labeled as the available 2025 edition; its Section 1256 discussion is a reason to keep records and obtain individual tax advice, not a blanket classification of every index option. |
| Course and simulator catalog | Source descriptions were aligned to the providers' exact pages: [IBKR course catalog](https://www.interactivebrokers.com/campus/traders-academy/finance-courses/), [OIC tools](https://www.optionseducation.org/options-quotes-calculators), and [CME simulator FAQ](https://www.cmegroup.com/articles/faqs/trading-simulator-faq.html). The library now states CME practice data are delayed and its simulator does not automatically settle open positions at expiry. [IBKR documents paper-fill limitations](https://www.ibkrguides.com/orgportal/aboutpapertradingaccount.htm); the research lab no longer treats simulated fills as live execution calibration. |
| Execution-cost research | One former citation did not support its claim. The lab now cites [Muravyev and Pearson](https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/33/11/4973/5732665) for the difference between quoted and effective spreads and [de Silva, So, and Smith](https://academic.oup.com/rof/article-abstract/30/2/489/8301159) for high retail option costs around earnings. These findings do not supply a universal fill assumption. |
| Historical data and backtests | [Cboe DataShop's EOD product](https://datashop.cboe.com/option-eod-summary) supports 15:45 and end-of-day snapshots, with optional Greeks calculated at 15:45; fields, quote sizes, and underlying index licenses require product-specific checking. The [backtest-overfitting paper](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2326253) supports logging strategy selection and testing on untouched data. The [NBER option-premium paper](https://www.nber.org/papers/w31833) reports narrowing premia over the last 15 years of a sample ending in 2022; the course now states the sample boundary rather than implying a timeless or current trading edge. |

## Remaining limits

1. **Paid and account-gated content:** We verified public catalog and product descriptions, not Cboe's registered learning portal, an IBKR account, ORATS subscriptions, OptionMetrics, or a purchased Cboe historical dataset. Actual tools, fields, prices, and access can differ by account and license.
2. **Cboe historical coverage discrepancy:** [Cboe's product pages](https://datashop.cboe.com/option-eod-summary) and [FAQ](https://datashop.cboe.com/faqs) present different historical start dates. The course makes no start-date promise; confirm the exact symbol, dates, fields, and quote-size conventions with Cboe before purchase.
3. **Broker and personal circumstances:** We cannot verify a particular broker's current permissions, house margin, exercise cutoff, fills, fees, or the learner's tax treatment without account-specific information. Those checks are explicit gates in the course.
4. **Course effectiveness:** No public source can verify that this exact curriculum will make a particular person profitable or “the world's best.” The course's assessments measure knowledge, process, and research quality; live performance would need a long, independently checked record across market regimes.

These corrections describe the version reviewed at the time of this source audit. Later course expansions are recorded below. When a source changes, update the relevant claim and the checked date rather than relying on this report indefinitely.

## Teaching-volume addendum — October 26, 2026

After this source audit, the syllabus was expanded into [four teaching volumes](README.md) with **26 prose lessons, 104 specific weekly plans, exercises and answer keys, and a gate for every module** (about 25,000 words of teaching material). The beginner chapters were checked against SEC/OCC/OIC/FINRA/Cboe sources; the behavior chapters against OIC/Cboe/IBKR; and the quantitative chapters against Khan Academy, MIT, OCC, and Cboe. Both runnable Python examples in Volume 3 were executed and their outputs checked. The research volume received an independent review that corrected its BXM data-access example, defined slippage to avoid double counting, and made forward shadow logging continuous from week 85 onward. All local links in the expanded project resolve.

The exercises have not been trialed with a new learner. Their pass standards test understanding and process, not a demonstrated ability to earn live trading profits.

## Practice-system expansion — October 26, 2026

The course now includes a [math diagnostic and bridge](FOUNDATION_MATH_BRIDGE.md), [40-case payoff bank](FOUNDATION_ASSESSMENTS.md) with a [separate key](FOUNDATION_ANSWER_KEY.md) and [changed-number generator](scripts/generate_foundation_cases.py), full [operational cases](OPERATIONAL_CASEBOOK.md), [execution replay](EXECUTION_PRACTICE.md), [discrete hedge ledger](DYNAMIC_HEDGING_LAB.md), [runnable synthetic labs](labs/README.md), a [learning record](LEARNING_RECORD_TEMPLATE.md), and [three later path standards](MASTERY_TRACKS.md). [The starting record](MY_LEARNING_RECORD.md) uses the learner's self-reported Python, options, and math experience; its pending assessments are not recorded as passes. The course map and research lab now distinguish software validation, published-index analysis, and licensed historical contract replay before selecting a capstone.

**Implementation checks:** The 40 supplied payoff-answer rows were independently recalculated from their strikes, premiums, fees, and final stock prices. The worked operational, order, and hedge ledgers received independent arithmetic review. The fresh-case generator produced separate question and answer files for two seeds, with 40 distinct rows each and changed questions across seeds. The `labs/` teaching program runs on its bundled synthetic fixture; **17 automated accounting, model, data-quality, timing, and research checks pass**. The local-link checker in [scripts/check_materials.py](scripts/check_materials.py) resolves **231 local links across 22 Markdown files**. Both embedded Volume 3 Python demonstrations were run during the revision. The toy option backtest preserves nonfills and a position left open when the exit quote is unavailable.

**Limits of this check:** The bundled prices, fills, P&L, and forecasts are invented and show only whether the code follows its stated assumptions. This revision did not buy historical contract data, access a live brokerage account, measure live execution, or trial the expanded course with a new learner. The prior external-source audit above describes its original scope; the new internal link and code checks are not a fresh verification of every external course, book, fee, or broker rule. Before a real product or data purchase, check current OCC, exchange, broker, and vendor information again. A completed synthetic or published-index capstone supplies no direct evidence that an executable options strategy will be profitable.

title: Options course verification report
body:
# Options course verification report

**Review date: November 14, 2026.** This report covers the existing course, the new 64-lesson beginner path and the full-stack learning app. Three parallel reviews examined foundations, advanced material and executable labs. These are internal technical reviews, not accreditation or an external audit of trading performance.

**Current update:** a subsequent full audit identified 14 defects and a dependency advisory register. The appended audit-corrections section records the fixes and current verification results. Earlier test counts below retain the scope of the initial review.

## Course findings and corrections

| Area | Finding and action |
| --- | --- |
| Starting from zero | The previous default was 104 weeks at 10 hours weekly and introduced many terms in the first sitting. The main path now has 64 micro lessons for 10–15 minute sessions. The long curriculum remains an optional advanced route. |
| Prerequisites | Removed the unsupported assumption that the learner can already program. Coding and calculus are not required for the beginner path. |
| Purchased options at expiry | Added exercise-by-exception and the possibility of a share purchase or short-stock position, with separate funding and subsequent share risk. A premium-loss bound for an option is not a bound on a stock position created by exercise. |
| Closing versus writing | Taught sell-to-close versus sell-to-open early, then repeated it in the lifecycle module. Selling an owned option does not by itself mean opening a short option. |
| Execution casebook | Corrected the description from three to four replay episodes. |
| Practice access | Clarified IBKR's funded regular paper-account workflow versus its separate trial; notebook simulation requires no broker account or deposit. Removed a CME course lesson count that could not be confirmed from its public page. |
| Advanced policy | Made the full research gates an optional extended training policy, rather than a prerequisite for all beginner learning goals. No course quiz automatically authorizes live trading. |
| Source dates | Preserved October 26 verification history separately; no old catalog or paid-data check was silently relabeled as newly completed. |

The foundation review recomputed the written long/short call and put examples and 40-case answer bank; no numerical corrections were needed. The advanced review checked worked strategy, Greek, hedge and assignment examples under their stated assumptions. New examples and capstone ledgers were recomputed.
